title: From Procedures to Permissions: Learning Precise Subagent Authorization from Agent Skills
abstract: arXiv:2611.08905v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: As language agents tackle increasingly complex tasks, they increasingly rely on multiple agents to coordinate specialized work, requiring decisions not only about what each subagent should do but also which tools and workspace resources it should access. Existing agent systems provide mechanisms for controlling tools and execution environments, but do not directly specify the resources required by each delegated subtask. Moreover, task outcomes and execution trajectories alone provide limited supervision for determining whether a subagent has received appropriate permissions. We observe that Agent Skills encode procedural knowledge describing the operations, tools, and files required at each step, providing a natural source of supervision for authorization. translated_title: 从流程到权限：从智能体技能中学习精确的子智能体授权
translated_abstract: 随着语言智能体处理日益复杂的任务，它们越来越多地依赖多个智能体来协调专业化工作，这不仅需要决定每个子智能体应该做什么，还需要决定它应该访问哪些工具和工作区资源。现有的智能体系统提供了控制工具和执行环境的机制，但并未直接指定每个被委派子任务所需的资源。此外，仅凭任务结果和执行轨迹，难以为判断子智能体是否获得了适当权限提供充分的监督信号。我们观察到，智能体技能编码了描述每一步所需操作、工具和文件的过程性知识，为授权提供了天然的监督来源。基于这一观察，我们从技能中合成任务和分步流程，在交互环境中通过子智能体委派来执行这些任务，并利用经过验证的轨迹……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出将Agent Skills中编码的过程性知识（即每一步所需的操作、工具和文件信息）作为天然监督信号，通过从技能合成任务并在交互环境中以子智能体委派方式执行，来学习为子智能体授予精确的工具与工作区资源权限。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes leveraging the procedural knowledge encoded in Agent Skills—which specifies the operations, tools, and files required at each step—as natural supervision for authorization, by synthesizing tasks from Skills and executing them through subagent delegation in interactive environments to learn precise tool and workspace resource permissions for subagents.
